item.title: 'DNA origami' could be key for making an effective HIV vaccine, early study hints
item.description: A new vaccine design uses folded DNA to steer the immune system toward producing the rare immune cells needed to make protective antibodies against HIV.

item.title: Antarctica 'ghost particle' observatory gets major upgrade that could 'pave the way' to physics breakthroughs
item.description: The National Science Foundation's massive IceCube neutrino detector at the South Pole just got a major new upgrade, which promises to take the search for "ghost particles" to a new level.

item.title: China's carbon emissions may have reached a critical turning point sooner than expected
item.description: The carbon emissions of the world's biggest greenhouse gas emitter have plateaued for nearly two years.

item.title: Capture 2026's space and astronomy highlights with one of our favorite astrophotography cameras — the Sony Alpha 7 IV has 20% off at Amazon
item.description: Our camera expert Kimberley Lane gave the Sony Alpha 7 IV an almost flawless review, and it delivered incredibly well, not just for astrophotography but as a brilliant all-rounder.

item.title: Risk of death from pregnancy in the US is 44 times higher than that from abortion, new analysis reveals
item.description: A figure commonly used to compare the risk of death from pregnancy compared with the risk of death from abortion might be based on outdated data, a new study suggests.

item.title: Astronomers discover 'unique inside-out system' with a rocky planet far from where it belongs
item.description: Astronomers have spotted an unusual 'inside-out' planetary system where a rocky world seems to have formed far beyond the realm typically reserved for gas giants.

item.title: The earliest black holes in the universe may still be with us, surprising study claims
item.description: The earliest black holes in the universe may not have disappeared from Hawking radiation after all, new research hints. Instead, they fed on the energy of the ancient cosmos to grow supermassive.

item.title: China banned fishing in its biggest river, and species are starting to recover
item.description: Decades of overfishing and habitat degradation led to huge declines in freshwater biodiversity in China's longest river, but there are signs of recovery after a fishing ban was implemented in 2021.

item.title: Subterranean tunnel, possibly used for medieval cult rituals, discovered in Stone Age tomb in Germany
item.description: A tunnel system discovered in a Stone Age tomb in Germany suggests medieval people created hiding places for their cultic rituals.

item.title: NASA telescope spots the building blocks for life spewing out of comet 3I/ATLAS
item.description: NASA's SPHEREx space telescope detected organic molecules coming off comet 3I/ATLAS as the interstellar visitor made its closest approach to Earth in December.
